relevance_note: Single case report of a girl with sporadic Blau syndrome carrying a NOD2 variant: "A missense mutation, p.(R587C), was detected in her NOD2 gene, and she was diagnosed with SBS."
method_note: Hand extraction of a single case report; no tables. One in-scope person (label 'patient', rule 5). Previously published patients in the Discussion (e.g. 'all 3 Blau syndrome patients carrying p.(R587C) mutation' in Rose et al. [15]; cohort figures from refs [12]-[14]) are mentioned only as counts or group-level statements without identifiable individuals and get no rows. Inheritance left 'not reported': the authors call the variant de novo but state that family members were not genetically tested (rule 8 / D-24). Zygosity not stated. Pathogenicity not stated beyond 'missense mutation'. Contradiction: Case Presentation says 'She had no pain in her right ankle' while the Discussion says 'pain was minimal'; both rows emitted (pain is not a checklist item). 'No eye involvement' was recorded on admission at 11 years; bilateral panuveitis developed later (after methotrexate cessation at 16), so both are recorded with timing; checklist uveitis = observed. 'Blood chemistry was unremarkable' and 'Urine tests were normal' are whole-investigation statements, recorded as written and used to exclude nothing more specific. 'Antinuclear antibody was borderline' recorded as neither observed nor excluded. Checklist 'arthritis or joint synovitis' left 'not reported': recurrent joint swelling with effusion is reported, but the paper explicitly says there was no synovitis and never calls her joint lesion arthritis (only the later-revised sJIA diagnosis); joint swelling and no-synovitis rows are in phenotypic_features. 'Visual impairment or blindness' left 'not reported' ('foggy' vision and 'visual acuity recovered' imply but do not state impaired acuity). 'No hilar lymphadenopathy' does not exclude the broader 'lymphadenopathy' item. Ages at SBS diagnosis and at last evaluation are not stated (methotrexate stopped at 16; uveitis 12 months later). Ethnicity not stated. first_author taken as 'Imayoshi' from the header 'Imayoshi Miyoko' (surname-first order assumed).

treatment_summary.value: aspirin; bolus methylprednisolone, then prednisolone, ibuprofen and methotrexate (methotrexate discontinued at 16 years); after panuveitis, methotrexate restarted, prednisolone increased and infliximab added (effective; prednisolone reduced to 4 mg/day)
span: Although she started aspirin, the intermittent fever continued.
Bolus methylprednisolone (1 g/day for 3 days), followed by prednisolone (1 mg/kg/day), ibuprofen (30 mg/kg/day), and methotrexate (15 mg/m^2/week), was started
When she was 16 years old, we discontinued methotrexate to avoid its adverse effects on the lungs.
Methotrexate was restarted, and the dosage of prednisolone was increased soon after her panuveitis was diagnosed
she was additionally treated with infliximab (4 mg/kg). Infliximab was extremely effective, and her visual acuity recovered
